title: A retired worker can mutate a successor lease when task identity is reused

teacher.evidence: Independent local code review and executed Python reproductions during this session

source.teacher: Codex collaborative agent /root/codex_teacher; actual session model identity not exposed as public API metadata

invariant: A worker whose acquisition expired or was released must not renew, finish, or release a later acquisition, even if campaign and candidate identifiers match.
preconditions: Two worker executions can use the same campaign and candidate identifiers
The original worker survives expiration or release while a replacement acquires the input

steps.action: claim same input, campaign, candidate with lease_seconds=10
renew returns False, confirming original lease has expired
claim the same logical identity returns claimed=True and reason=reclaimed
renew its lease and inspect observation count

root_cause: Ownership is checked only by campaign/candidate names and lease_until. No acquisition generation identifies which attempt owns that row, so reusing names revives stale write authority.

controls.positive: Repeat the retired worker finish against a fresh temporary SQLite store twice
controls.negative: Change only the replacement candidate identifier; the stale finish is rejected and replacement remains live

fix.behavior: Each successful claim rotates a unique acquisition token; renew, finish and release compare the token. Engine explicitly forwards the token. Sequential legacy callers use the latest token cached on their own instance.
fix.compatibility_limit: Same-instance concurrent acquisitions must pass lease_token explicitly; the implicit cache only represents the latest claim on that instance.

lesson.teacher: Codex collaborative agent /root/codex_teacher, independently executed Python reproduction
preconditions: Durable ownership can expire and later be reacquired.
Different executions may reuse the same logical identity.
search_strategy: Distinguish the identity of a logical task from the identity of one acquisition attempt.
Keep the earlier worker alive after ending its ownership, then acquire a successor lease from another connection.
Test whether an operation from the earlier worker changes the successor's state.
Use distinct successor identities as a paired control, and compare multiple lifecycle transitions and operations.
lesson.oracle: A retired attempt must not regain mutation rights merely because its logical names reappear. Check persisted state and the successor's ownership, not only a returned status.
nonexamples: A still-active attempt renewing its own acquisition is valid.
A new attempt claiming after expiry is valid; acceptance of a stale attempt is the defect.
A local deterministic lease test does not establish a hosted model behavior.
lesson.scope: External-memory instruction, no model weight update; frozen pre-fix code.

student_assessment.heldout_requirement: Change ownership lifecycle and stale operation; renaming values is insufficient
student_assessment.live_student_status: Not run by this teacher; main-thread runner owns actual Nemotron evaluation

limitations: This proves local framework lease correctness behavior, not a hosted model vulnerability
Teaching uses frozen pre-fix production code and clearly labels that scope
Production repair has local regression evidence; cross-process mixed-version deployments are not supported by this test
